html:
In the early hours of 1 November 1954, the National Liberation Front (FLN) launched a series of attacks on police posts, army barracks and farms across Algeria, with the heaviest in the Aurès mountains. It was the start of the Algerian War.

The FLN had been founded weeks before by young militants who had broken with the older nationalist leader Messali Hadj. Its declaration called for an independent Algeria. The attacks were small and killed only a few people, and France at first treated them as banditry. The interior minister, François Mitterrand, said Algeria was France.

But the revolt spread, and the war lasted almost eight years. November 1 is Algeria's national revolution day. See also Sétif.
